The present proceedings are instituted under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeking quashing of FIR No.
209/2022 registered under Sections 420/406/120B/328/34 IPC at P.S. Crime Branch, Delhi on the ground that the parties have amicably settled their disputes.
2. The allegations in the present FIR relate to fraud and forgery committed by the petitioners causing loss to respondent No.2 to the tune of Rs.51,21,735/-.
3. Mr. Singh, learned APP for the State, on instructions, submits that the petitioners are the only accused person and respondent No.2 is the complainant/victim.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners and respondent No. 2 have amicably settled their disputes out of Court.

sentences.text:
The broad principles which emerge from the precedents on the subject, may be summarised in the following propositions:
xxx 16.7.
As distinguished from serious offences, there may be criminal cases which have an overwhelming or predominant element of a civil dispute.

They stand on a distinct footing in so far as the exercise of the inherent power to quash is concerned;
16.8.
In such a case, the High Court may quash the criminal proceeding if in view of the compromise between the disputants, This is a digitally signed order.

9. Similarly, in State of Madhya Pradesh v. Laxmi Narayan and Others reported as (2019) 5 SCC 403, it has been held as under:-
"15.

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Laxmi Narayan and Others reported as (2019) 5 SCC 403
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering the law on the point and the other decisions of this Court on the point, referred to hereinabove, it is observed and held as under:
15.1.

That the power conferred Under Section 482 of the Code to quash the criminal proceedings for the non-compoundable offences Under Section 320 of the Code can be exercised having overwhelmingly and predominantly the civil character,
particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes and when the parties have resolved the entire dispute amongst themselves;"
